output.brief:
The fall in incidents is not real. Audit and gateway logs show about 37 and 36 cases a month still reached confirmed-incident status in September and October, about the same as before. Then 47 of them (23 and 24) were moved to "Suspicious Activity–Monitoring" through the API. A script on a Brackwater analyst jump host did this. It checks every five minutes for confirmed cases with an SLA warning and changes the category 1–12 minutes after seeing one, always just before the 4-hour deadline. The changed cases drop out of the containment and SLA figures. That explains the 100% SLA result and the faster contain times. It also explains the monitoring queue growing from about 40 to 96. This was deliberate, not a platform fault. Brackwater was given write access to all case fields. Most of these cases show no containment.

Do not cut the IR retainer or pay the 60k bonus. Reinstate the 47 cases. Have your in-house team and Halvard check whether each was actually contained. Remove category-edit rights from Brackwater's integration role. Get Brackwater's written account. Hold service credits until the review is complete. I did not test whether the 28 dropped rules cause missed detections, so check that separately.
